title: Bay Area Open Science Group - Meet MySuppleHub: An Open, Community-Contributed Evidence Base for Dietary Supplements
description:
This month we are joined by Kelly Yoo and Meenu Krishnakumar from Stanford, who will discuss their work on MySuppleHub. Over half of US adults use dietary supplements, yet the evidence supporting many products remains fragmented, uneven in quality, and often influenced by industry funding. MySuppleHub, developed by the Snyder Lab in the Department of Genetics at Stanford, approaches this problem as an open science opportunity. The platform combines a citation-linked supplement encyclopedia with community surveys, polls, and self-reported experiences, creating a shared evidence base in which participants can both contribute their experiences and benefit from a growing body of accessible, evidence-informed information.

The Bay Area Open Science Group is a growing community for Bay Area academics and researchers interested in incorporating open science into their research, teaching, and learning. Targeting students, faculty, and staff at UCSF, Berkeley, and Stanford, the goal of the community is to increase awareness of and engagement with all things open science, including open access articles, open research data, open source software, and open educational resources. Through this work the group hopes to connect researchers with tools they can use to make the products and process of science more equitable and reproducible.

UCSF welcomes all participants to our events. If you need a reasonable accommodation to participate in this event because of a disability, please contact Ariel Deardorff at ariel.deardorff@ucsf.edu as soon as possible.

title: UCSF Industry Documents Library Introduction to the Firearms Archive
description:
Join us for an introduction to the Firearms Industry Documents Archive (FAIDA), co-hosted by the Industry Documents Library (IDL) and the Firearms Accountability Initiative (FAI). We’ll discuss how to navigate the new FAIDA archive, and IDL archivists will be available to answer your research questions.

The Firearms Accountability Initiative (FAI) is a collaborative, nonpartisan effort to transform the gun violence epidemic by making firearm deaths and injuries the gun industry’s problem. FAI seeks to catalyze accountability in the courtroom and in the court of public opinion, challenging the behavior of reckless firearm industry actors that endanger our communities.

Accessibility: UCSF welcomes all participants to our events. If you need a reasonable accommodation to participate in this event because of a disability, please contact Melissa Ignacio by emailing melissa.ignacio2@ucsf.edu as soon as possible.

Register at https://ucsf.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_US0e8CqtRuWCL6ONBu-CiQ#/registration

This session will be recorded.

Background information: In August 2026, IDL published a new Firearms Industry Document Archive (FAIDA) of nearly 700 documents. The documents were obtained during Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison's 2022 lawsuit, which alleged that Fleet Farm, a 50-store chain that sells firearms, hunting equipment, and other goods in five Midwest states, negligently sold firearms to straw buyers (people who purchase firearms on behalf of another person) and contributed to gun trafficking in Minnesota. One of the guns sold to a straw purchaser was later fired in a mass shooting, which killed one person and injured 14. Under the February 2026 settlement, Fleet Farm agreed to significant policy changes to help prevent straw purchases, pay a $1 million penalty, and publicly release the records that are now in FAIDA.

For more information and to view the documents, visit https://www.industrydocuments.ucsf.edu/firearms/collections/fleet-farm-collection/

title: AI Discussion Club: Are we in an AI bubble? Vapid vs. meaningful AI integration
description:
Thinking about artificial intelligence? Whether you're nervous or excited about AI, whether you're normally a talker or chat-lurker, join us for this online discussion session where we discuss 2-3 articles, videos, or news pieces about AI. We will use Padlet as a primary source of idea-sharing, but there will also be opportunities for participants to share via Zoom chat or hand-raising depending on preference.

 

The reading/watching commitment for this series is relatively light (15-30 min of content), and discussion questions will be shared with registrants before the session. Reading/watching assigned content in advance and taking some notes is recommended, but not required for participation.

 

Readings

  • Ford, P. (2025, October 27). The Argument for Letting AI Burn It All Down. Wired. https://www.wired.com/story/ai-normal-after-ai-plateaus/
  • MIT Sloan Office of Communicatinos. (2026, September 9). Why some organizations turn AI experiments into business value while others quietly fail. MIT Sloan. https://mitsloan.mit.edu/press/why-some-organizations-turn-ai-experiments-business-value-while-others-quietly-fail

Optional:

  • Dreyfuss, E. (2026, August 7). San Francisco AI billboards: Why cryptic tech ads are alienating the city. The San Francisco Standard. https://sfstandard.com/pacific-standard-time/2026/08/07/sf-ai-billboards-dystopian-not-funny/

title: Open Source GenAI with Ollama
description:
Session Overview 

Ollama is an open-source platform that makes it possible to download and run generative AI (GenAI) models directly on your laptop or workstation. With Ollama, you can run a variety of open-source AI models for tasks such as basic chat, text analysis, audio transcription, and image recognition. Because these models run locally on your computer rather than through a cloud-based service such as ChatGPT or Gemini, Ollama can give you more control over where and how your data is processed.

In this workshop, we’ll introduce Ollama and explore the kinds of AI models you can download and run locally. We’ll discuss the benefits and limitations of local AI and when it might be useful for your work. We’ll also demonstrate how to use locally running models to analyze text and images with Python and Unix command-line tools.

No Python or Unix experience is required. This workshop is designed to be accessible and useful for participants with a range of technical backgrounds. Participants with Python or command-line experience are welcome to code along with the demonstrations, but coding is optional and not required to participate.

Learning Objectives

  • Explain the benefits and limitations of running open-source AI models locally.
  • Identify situations in which a local GenAI model might be useful for your work.
  • Describe the types of open-source AI models available through Ollama for working with text, audio, and images.
  • Understand how Ollama can be used to download and run AI models on a local computer.
  • For participants interested in hands-on coding, use Python and command-line tools to interact with a locally running model for basic text and image analysis.

description:

title: UCSF Industry Documents Library Annual Workshop
description:
The Annual Tobacco and Other Industry Documents Workshop, a free, online workshop hosted by UCSF’s Center for Tobacco Control Research and Education and the UCSF Industry Documents Library, will take place November 17-18, 2026 from 9-11 a.m. Pacific Time.

Registration: https://www.eventbrite.com/e/ucsf-industry-documents-library-workshop-tickets-2002093608879
Sign up for one day or both.

Day One: UCSF researchers and community partners will provide an overview of the Truth Tobacco Industry Documents and other collections, sharing real-world examples of how these documents have shaped tobacco control efforts over the past two decades.

Day Two: Industry Documents Library archivists will host an interactive session to demonstrate how you can navigate the library’s extensive resources, modify and organize searches, and get real-time support and tips from current document researchers.

Don’t miss this opportunity to learn how to use the documents that have driven groundbreaking public health policy change!

title: Document Classification with Python, AI and Machine Learning
description:

This workshop will provide hands-on instruction in using pre-trained machine learning models and GenAI models to summarize text,  classify documents, and find hidden topic patterns. We will use a combination of pre-trained models from HuggingFace, general classification models from cloud providers, and local GenAI based classification and summarization applications.

title: Bay Area Open Science Group - OpenADMET - Raising the bar on ADMET prediction with open science
description:
This month, Dr. Pat Walters is joining us to talk about the OpenADMET initiative. Drug discovery programs frequently stall due to the Avoid-ome, which comprises the complex off-target interactions and ADMET liabilities that traditional heuristic methods struggle to address. To solve this, OpenADMET combines high-resolution structural biology, directed data generation, and machine learning into a systematic framework for predicting and mitigating these liabilities. Central to this mission is generating targeted datasets to host large-scale blind benchmarks that test community predictive models on real-world drug design problems. By uniting hundreds of academic and industry teams through these challenges, webinars, and conferences, the initiative fosters widespread collaboration to establish transparent, data-driven standards across the field.
 
The Bay Area Open Science Group is a growing community for Bay Area academics and researchers interested in incorporating open science into their research, teaching, and learning. Targeting students, faculty, and staff at UCSF, Berkeley, and Stanford, the goal of the community is to increase awareness of and engagement with all things open science, including open access articles, open research data, open source software, and open educational resources. Through this work the group hopes to connect researchers with tools they can use to make the products and process of science more equitable and reproducible.
